title: Grade 12 Biology Comprehensive Exam 2018 (6 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 6 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText:
Two modern food processing companies use microorganisms in different ways.

Company I - produces high quality yogurt using Lactobacillus

Company II - produces bread by adding yeast to the dough
Which biotechnological role is shared by both companies?
options: Preventing spoilage completely in all condition
Increasing the yield but decreasing quality of the products
Improving test and texture through fermentation
questions.explanation: Both yogurt production using Lactobacillus and bread production using yeast rely on fermentation to enhance the flavor, taste, and structural texture of the food product.

questions.questionText: Which of the following sets of benefits can be gained from transgenic organisms?
options: Increased genetic diversity, improved carcass composition and susceptibility to diseases
High quality fiber, increased growth rate and improved milk composition
Increased feed utilization, decreased prolificacy and increased meat quality
High quality hair, increased susceptibility to disease and increased reproductive performance
questions.explanation: Transgenic organisms are genetically modified to provide desirable traits such as higher quality fiber, accelerated growth rates, and enhanced milk or muscle composition.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about bioremediation? It is the use of
options: fungi to eliminate insects that devastate food crops.
microbes to detoxify pollutants from the environments.
genetically modified microbes to extract minerals from their ores.
transgenic bacterium to improve growth rate and yield of crop.
questions.explanation: Bioremediation specifically refers to the application of biological organisms (microorganisms) to degrade, detoxify, or remove environmental contaminants and pollutants.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following procedures demonstrate the correct sequence of events that happen during replication a bacteriophage?
options: Synthesis of new molecules → attachment → entry of virions → assembly → release
Entry of virions → attachment → assembly → synthesis of new molecules → release
Attachment → entry of virions → synthesis of new molecules → assembly → release
Synthesis of new molecules → attachment → entry of virions → assembly → release
questions.explanation: The lytic cycle of a bacteriophage follows the sequence: Attachment (adsorption), Entry (penetration) of viral nucleic acid, Synthesis of viral components, Assembly of new virions, and Release via cell lysis.

questions.questionText: A student sterilized culture media, hospital needles for disposal and blood serum using different sterilization techniques. At the end of the experiment, she confirmed that all of the sterilized materials were germ free. Which sterilization techniques were used by the student, respectively?
options: Hot air oven, intermittent sterilization and flaming
Low temperature pasteurization, hot air oven and disinfection
Moist heat sterilization, incineration and intermittent sterilization
Tyndallization, dry heat sterilization and incineration
questions.explanation: Culture media is typically sterilized using moist heat (autoclaving/moist heat sterilization), disposable hospital needles via incineration, and heat-sensitive liquids like serum using intermittent sterilization (tyndallization) or filtration.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct sequences of events of bacterial reproduction by binary fission?
options: Replication of DNA → invagination of cell wall and membrane → formation of cross wall → two identical cells
Replication of DNA → invagination of cell wall and membrane → formation of cross wall → two different cells
Invagination of cell wall and membrane → Replication of DNA → formation of cross wall → two different cells
Invagination of cell wall and membrane → Replication of DNA → formation of cross wall → two identical cells
questions.explanation: Binary fission begins with the replication of bacterial DNA, followed by the inward growth/invagination of the cell membrane and wall, forming a septum/cross wall that splits the bacterium into two genetically identical daughter cells.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct regarding anabolic and catabolic pathways? Anabolic pathways
options: needs energy to synthesize macromolecules whereas catabolic pathways release energy from breakdown of molecules.
occur in mitochondria whereas the catabolic pathways occur in the chloroplasts.
provide raw materials for catabolic reactions whereas catabolic pathways use it to make larger molecules.
involve enzymes for chemical reactions whereas catabolic pathways use chemical catalysts.
questions.explanation: Anabolic pathways are endergonic and consume energy to construct complex macromolecules, whereas catabolic pathways are exergonic and break down complex molecules to release energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the reduction stage of the calvin cycle?
options: Combination of 3-phosphoglyceric acid with carbon dioxide
Combination of carbon dioxide to ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate
questions.explanation: During the reduction stage of the Calvin cycle, 3-PGA is converted into glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P) using ATP and NADPH, which ultimately leads to the formation of carbohydrates like glucose.

questions.questionText: If a plant is placed in a highly controlled environment where light is available but very limited CO₂, what will happen to the light-dependent and light-independent reactions of the photosynthesis?
options: The light dependent reaction produces ATP and NADPH while the light independent reaction will consume ATP.
The light independent reactions will continue while light dependent reaction will cease.
Light dependent reaction will stop producing oxygen, but light independent reaction will continue producing glucose.
Both the light-independent and light-dependent reaction will stop immediately.
questions.explanation: Light remains available, so light-dependent reactions continue generating ATP and NADPH. The light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) continue consuming ATP to fix what limited CO₂ is present, though glucose production rate slows down dramatically.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the process of Kreb's cycle? It begins with combination of acetyl-CoA with
options: pyruvate and ends with regeneration of oxaloacetate.
pyruvate and ends with generation of citric acids.
oxaloacetate and ends with regeneration of oxaloacetate.
oxaloacetate and ends with generation of citric acids.
questions.explanation: The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) begins when acetyl-CoA (2C) combines with oxaloacetate (4C) to form citrate (6C). Because it is a metabolic cycle, it concludes by regenerating oxaloacetate to start the cycle again with another acetyl-CoA molecule.

questions.questionText: How many net ATP molecules are produced from two glucose molecules assuming that only glycolysis is occurred due to shortage of oxygen?
questions.explanation: A single molecule of glucose yields a net gain of 2 ATP molecules during glycolysis. Therefore, under anaerobic conditions (shortage of oxygen), two glucose molecules will yield 2 × 2 = 4 net ATP molecules.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following table that shows complete oxidation of one glucose molecule in eukaryotic cells.

Which alternative contains the numbers corresponding to the correct comparison between the substrate level and oxidative phosphorylation?
questions.explanation: Statement III is correct because substrate-level phosphorylation occurs independently of oxygen (e.g., during glycolysis), whereas oxidative phosphorylation requires oxygen as the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain. Statement IV is correct because substrate-level phosphorylation directly transfers a high-energy phosphate group from a substrate to ADP, whereas oxidative phosphorylation relies on a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements explains how comparative anatomy provides evidence for evolution? Organisms having
options: the same structures but different functions had evolved from different ancestors.
analogous structure had shared a common ancestor.
different vestigial organs had evolved from the same ancestor.
pentadactyl limbs had evolved from a common ancestor.
questions.explanation: The pentadactyl limb (a five-digit limb structure found in humans, bats, whales, and lizards) is a classic example of a homologous structure. Even though these limbs serve different functions, their underlying anatomical similarity provides evidence that these organisms diverged from a common ancestor.

questions.questionText:
Four groups of students debated on the theories of the origin of life as indicated blow.

Group I - Explained the idea that the source of life on Earth was resistant spores from other planets.

Group II - Supported the idea that life started on earth as a result of divine intervention.

Group III - Supported the idea that life has no beginning or an end.

Group IV - Explained that life on earth began through chemical reactions.

Based on the above information, which theories were presented and debated on by group I, II, III and IV students, respectively?
options: Biochemical origin, special creationism, cosmozoan and eternity of life
Cosmozoan, special creationism, eternity of life and biochemical origin
Eternity of life, biochemical origin, abiogenesis and spontaneous generation
Abiogenesis, special creationism, cosmozoan and eternity of life
questions.explanation: Group I describes the Cosmozoan (Panspermia) theory, Group II describes Special Creationism, Group III describes the Eternity of Life theory, and Group IV describes the Biochemical Origin theory.

questions.questionText: During the field visit to a forest a student noticed that the population of beetles having short, medium, and long antennae were equally distributed previously. But over several generation, the beetles having medium antenna were significantly reduced and the allele frequencies of the other two groups increased. Which type of natural selection occurred in this beetle population?
questions.explanation: Disruptive selection favors extreme phenotypes (short and long antennae) over intermediate phenotypes (medium antennae), causing the population to split toward the two extremes.

questions.questionText: Suppose the frequency of the dominant allele in a given population is 0.8. What will be the frequency of the heterozygous genotype considering the condition of the Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Given p = 0.8 (dominant allele frequency), q = 1 - 0.8 = 0.2 (recessive allele frequency). The frequency of the heterozygous genotype (2pq) is 2 × 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.32.

questions.questionText:
An archeological survey conducted in four different sites revealed fossils of different members of the human family as indicated below.

Site I - Homo habilis

Site II - Australopithecus africanus

Site III - Homo sapiens

Site IV - Homo erectus

From the above information, which sequence shows the human family from the most primitive to the advanced?
questions.explanation: The evolutionary order from most primitive to most advanced is Australopithecus africanus (II) → Homo habilis (I) → Homo erectus (IV) → Homo sapiens (III).

questions.questionText: Which ions should enter the presynaptic and postsynaptic nerve cells in order for a nerve impulse to cross the synaptic cleft, respectively?
questions.explanation: Calcium ions (Ca²⁺) enter the presynaptic terminal to trigger neurotransmitter release, and sodium ions (Na⁺) enter the postsynaptic cell to induce depolarization.

questions.questionText: While cooking a pancake, a girl accidentally touched the hot part of the plate and immediately withdrew her hand. Which one of the following impulse pathways shows the correct sequence of events during response to this stimulus?
options: Receptor → motor neuron → sensory neuron → brain → effector
Receptor → interneuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector
Receptor → interneuron → brain → motor neuron → effector
Receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector
questions.explanation: In a reflex arc, the signal goes from the receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord (via interneuron) → motor neuron → effector.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the main functions of hypodermis? It
options: serves as an insulation and energy storage.
produces skin pigment known as melanin.
provides a waterproof barrier and produces keratin.
questions.explanation: The hypodermis (subcutaneous layer) consists mainly of adipose tissue, which provides thermal insulation and energy storage.

questions.questionText: Which of the following eye structure and its function is correctly matched?
options: Pupil - controls the iris muscles to adjust the light into the eyes
Iris - controls the diameter of the lens by attaching to its opposite ends
Sclera - physically supports the internal structures of the eyes
Cornea - provides nourishment to the inner parts of the eyes
questions.explanation: The sclera is the tough, fibrous outer layer that gives shape and structural support to the eye.

questions.questionText: If you are spinning in a chair and instantly stop, you feel a sensation of imbalance. What does this explain?
options: Fluid in the ampullae continues to move but the sensory hairs signaling stops.
Fluids in the semicircular canals stop moving, but the sensory hairs continue signaling.
Fluids in the semicircular canals continues to moving and the sensory hairs also bend for signaling.
Fluids in the sacculus and utriculus move irregularly leading to false motion.
questions.explanation: When you stop spinning abruptly, inertia causes the endolymph fluid inside the semicircular canals to keep moving, which continues to bend the sensory hair cells and signal motion to the brain.

questions.questionText: Which one is directly related to the water-conserving role of the kidneys?
options: Their location in the body in relation to other organ-systems and their fat cover
Their internal structures specialized for absorption and reabsorption sequentially
Their feature having endocrine glands on the top of the kidneys
Their unique external shape, size, color and overall appearance
questions.explanation: The specialized internal microscopic structures of the kidney, specifically the nephron tubules and loop of Henle, enable selective reabsorption of water and solutes to conserve body water.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following events of the process of urine formation.

1. Descending loop of Henle allows water to pass from the filtrate into the intestinal fluid.

2. Collecting duct reabsorbs solutes and water from the filtrate.

3. Glomerulus filters small solutes from the blood.

4. Ascending loop of Henle reabsorbs Na and Cl from the filtrate into the intestinal fluid.

5. Proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs ions, water and nutrients, remove toxins and adjust filtrate pH.

6. Distal tubule selectively secretes and absorbs different ions to maintain blood pH and electrolyte balance.

Which one of the following options show the correct sequence of events mentioned above in the process of urine formation?
questions.explanation: The order of filtrate passage through the nephron is: Glomerulus (3) → Proximal Convoluted Tubule (5) → Descending Loop of Henle (1) → Ascending Loop of Henle (4) → Distal Tubule (6) → Collecting Duct (2).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following descriptions is correct about the structures of the nerve system?
options: The central nerve system is composed of brain and parasympathetic nerves.
The sensory neurons and the spinal cord constitute the peripheral nerve system.
Nerve system located in the spinal cord and sense organs are part of the peripheral nerve system.
Nerves in the brain and the spinal cord responsible for motor outputs are part of the central nerve system.
questions.explanation: The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord, which process information and initiate motor outputs through motor tracts/neurons residing within them.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following table that shows the functions of hormones produced by different endocrine glands.

Which alternative contains the numbers with the correct functions of the hormones in the above table?
questions.explanation: Row I is correct (Pituitary: ADH increases water reabsorption; Parathyroid: PTH increases calcium reabsorption; Adrenal: Epinephrine/Norepinephrine causes skin vasoconstriction). Row III is also correct (Pituitary: Oxytocin/Prolactin promotes milk release; Parathyroid: PTH stimulates osteoclasts to release calcium from bones; Adrenal: Glucocorticoids/Cortisol promote gluconeogenesis during fasting).

questions.questionText: In a hot summer, a person's body temperature rises above the normal level. Which pair of physiological thermoregulatory mechanisms adjust the body to the normal state?
questions.explanation: To lower elevated body temperature, the body triggers sweating (evaporative cooling) and vasodilation of cutaneous blood vessels (allowing more heat to radiate away from the skin surface).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements defines climate change? It refers to
options: short-term change in the temperature of an environment.
the daily weather change of a specific environment.
systematic change in the atmosphere over a long period.
the static weather change of an environment in a year.
questions.explanation: Climate change refers to long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns, which represent a systematic change in the atmosphere over an extended period.

questions.questionText:
An environmental impact assessment study was conducted in three countries to determine the contribution of human activities to the greenhouse effects.

Country I - Extensive use of industrial fertilizers for agriculture

Country II - Large scale use of rice paddies for agriculture

Country III - Huge amount of fossil fuel combustion for electricity

Based on the above information, which types of greenhouse gases were produced by country I, II, and III, respectively?
options: Methane, carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide
Nitrous oxide, methane and carbon dioxide
Sulfur hexafluoride, methane and nitrous oxide
questions.explanation: Industrial fertilizers release nitrous oxide, anaerobic decomposition in rice paddies produces methane, and fossil fuel combustion predominantly yields carbon dioxide.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements explains the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. It is an agreement that
options: provides permission for the developed countries to invest low carbon projects in the poorer countries.
forces developing countries to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions by 5%.
prohibits dangerous human interference with climate system.
obliges the industrialized nations to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions by half.
questions.explanation: The ultimate objective of the UNFCCC is to stabilize greenhouse gas concentrations at a level that prevents dangerous human (anthropogenic) interference with the climate system.

questions.questionText: Which of the following minerals is essential for the transport of oxygen in the blood?
questions.explanation: Iron is a central component of hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

questions.questionText: The hormone that causes the 'let-down' of milk during breastfeeding and triggers contractions during birth is:
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is often called the 'love hormone' and is crucial for social bonding and labor.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following features is NOT the characteristic feature of fungi? They
options: have haploid nuclei and multinucleate hypha.
are either autotrophic, parasitic or saprophytic.
exhibit apical growth of networked hypha.
questions.explanation:
Fungi are heterotrophic organisms; they cannot make their own food (not autotrophic).

 They obtain nutrients by absorption and are commonly parasitic or saprophytic. They typically have haploid nuclei, multinucleate hyphae, reproduce by spores, and show apical growth of hyphae.

questions.questionText: What are the common plants of the boreal forest?
questions.explanation: The boreal forest (Taiga) is dominated by cold-tolerant, cone-bearing trees known as conifers (e.g., spruce, fir).

questions.questionText: Which of the following diseases is caused by a DNA virus?
questions.explanation:
Cold sores are caused by the Herpes simplex virus, which is a DNA virus. 

The other viruses listed (Corona, Influenza, HIV) are RNA viruses.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of a learned behaviour?
questions.explanation:
Classical conditioning is a form of associative learned behaviour where an animal associates a previously neutral stimulus with a biologically significant one.

 The other options are examples of innate or fixed action patterns.

questions.questionText: What is the main difference between anabolism and catabolism in cellular metabolic pathways?Anabolism
options: absorbs energy while catabolism releases energy
is destructive while catabolism is constructive process
occurs during respiration while catabolism occurs in photosynthesis
breaks down macromolecules while catabolism buildsups them.
questions.explanation:
Anabolism consists of energy-consuming reactions that build complex molecules (e.g., proteins from amino acids), whereas catabolism consists of energy-releasing reactions that break down complex molecules (e.g., glucose into CO₂ and H₂O).

 This is the main difference between the two metabolic pathways.

questions.questionText: Which fungus is famously used for making bread and beer?
questions.explanation: This yeast ferments sugars into CO2 (to make bread rise) and ethanol (for beer).

questions.questionText: A 'Plasmid' is:
options: The liquid part of the blood
small, circular piece of DNA found in bacteria
questions.explanation: Plasmids are used in biotechnology as vectors to carry foreign genes into a host cell.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of in-sight learning?
options: Use of boxes, after several trials , by a chimpanzee placed in an enclosed area to obtain bananas placed on the top of an enclosure.
Salivation of a dog when a bell was rung in the absence of food, which was paired with the conditioned stimulus.
Lack of response from a lady, which sat in a shop in which a strong deodorant was continuously released from a can.
Exhibition of modifications of natural behaviors of guide dogs, horses or zoo animals to desired behaviors.
questions.explanation:
Insight learning is a form of cognitive learning where an animal solves a problem by suddenly understanding the relationships between parts, often without prior trial-and-error.
 The classic experiment involves a chimp using a tool (like stacking boxes to reach food) which is described in option A.

questions.questionText: Which organism is commonly used as a 'cell factory' to produce enzymes for the food industry?
questions.explanation: Microorganisms like yeast and bacteria are efficient and cheap to grow for mass-producing industrial enzymes.

questions.questionText: Which of these describes a 'saprophyte'?
options: An organism that eats living animals
An organism that feeds on dead organic matter
An organism that makes food from light
An organism that lives in a vacuum
questions.explanation: Many fungi and bacteria are saprophytes, helping to clean up the environment by breaking down dead things.

questions.questionText: Fresh water biomes like streams and rivers are characterized by the presence of
questions.explanation:
Freshwater biomes are characterized by organisms adapted to flowing water, including photosynthetic organisms like algae, floating organisms like plankton (phyto- and zoo-), and various species of fish.
 Corals, crabs, kelp, and angler fish are typically found in marine (saltwater) environments.

questions.questionText: Which statement shows the correct comparison between the Lamarck's and Darwin's theory of evolution?
options: Lamarck believed in the development of new traits due to variation while Darwin believed in their occurrence due to use and disuse of organs.
Darwin recognized the origin of species was through mutation while Lamarck believed it was through effect of the environment.
Lamarck believed the gradual occurrence of changes while Darwin believed in the immediate change of species.
Darwin claimed that variation is heritable while Lamarck considers variation as acquired traits.
questions.explanation:
Darwin's theory of natural selection relies on heritable variations in populations that confer survival advantages.

 Lamarck proposed that traits acquired during an organism's lifetime (e.g., through use or disuse) could be passed to offspring, which is now known to be incorrect.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements explain how nerve impulse is occurred? It occurs as a result of
options: charge difference across the membrane of axon.
The movement of neurotransmitter molecules into myelin sheath.
balanced charge across the membrane of dendrites.
The movement of neurotransmitter molecules out of cell body.
questions.explanation:
A nerve impulse, or action potential, is generated by a rapid, temporary change in the electrical potential across the axon membrane. 

This occurs due to the movement of ions (primarily Na+ and K+) across the membrane, creating A charge difference across the membrane of axon (depolarization and repolarization).

questions.questionText: The study of fungi is known as:
questions.explanation: Mycology is the branch of biology concerned with the study of fungi.

questions.questionText: Bacteria that require a high concentration of CO2 for growth are called:
questions.explanation: Capnophiles grow best in environments with 5-10% CO2, such as the respiratory tract.

questions.questionText: Gram-positive bacteria differ from Gram-negative bacteria primarily in that Gram-positives have:
options: thick layer of peptidoglycan and teichoic acids
thin peptidoglycan layer in the periplasmic space
questions.explanation: Gram-positive bacteria have a thick, multi-layered peptidoglycan cell wall that retains the crystal violet stain, along with teichoic acids.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a common example of a fungus?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms are the fruiting bodies of certain types of multicellular fungi.

questions.questionText: Which of these is an example of a viral 'envelope'?
options: The protein subunits of the capsid
lipid bilayer derived from the host cell membrane
The tail fibers of a T4 phage
questions.explanation: Enveloped viruses acquire a lipid bilayer from the host cell's plasma or nuclear membrane as they exit (bud) from the cell.

questions.questionText: Which of the following Protozoa moves using 'pseudopodia'?
questions.explanation: Amoeboid movement is characterized by the extension of the cytoplasm into temporary projections called pseudopodia ('false feet').

questions.questionText: Identify the correct mechanism of bacterial reproduction by conjugation.
options: Mitotic spindles are produced to separate bacterial DNA into two equal parts.
The recipient bacteria use their pili to pull the donor bacteria during plasmid transfer.
Bacteria take up genetic materials of dead organisms and integrate into their DNA.
pair of bacteria come together and exchanges their plasmids.
questions.explanation:
In bacterial conjugation, two bacterial cells connect through a conjugation pilus.

 The donor transfers plasmid DNA to the recipient, resulting in genetic exchange between the two bacteria.

questions.questionText: In binary fission, the cell first replicates its:
questions.explanation: The replication of the bacterial chromosome is the first and most critical step before the cell elongates and splits.

questions.questionText: If mRNA brings the code "UGA" into the ribosome
options: tRNA will bring the amino acid methionine.
translation ceases and protein synthesis terminates.
questions.explanation:
The mRNA codon UGA is a stop codon.
 Stop codons signal the termination of protein synthesis, so when UGA enters the ribosome, translation ceases and the newly formed protein is released.

questions.questionText: Which of the following lacks a cellular structure entirely?
questions.explanation: Viruses are acellular; they consist of genetic material in a protein coat and cannot function outside a host.

questions.questionText: In Human evolution brain size increased over the courses of evolution: Which alternative contains hominids arranged in an **increasing order of brain size**?
options: Homo neandertalensis --> Homo erecus --> Homo habilis --> Homo
Homo erceras --> Homo habilis --> Homo neandertalensis --> Homo sapiens
Homo erectus --> Homo Acandertalensis --> Homo habilis --> Homo
Homo habilis --> Homo erectus --> Homo neandertalensis --> Homo sapiens
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which of these is the term for spherical (round) bacteria?
questions.explanation: Cocci are round-shaped bacteria, like the ones that cause strep throat.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an 'Extreme Halophile'?
questions.explanation: Halobacterium is an archaeon that thrives in extremely high salt concentrations, such as the Dead Sea or Great Salt Lake.

questions.questionText: Which stage of the nitrogen cycle needs the role of Rhizobium?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium is a bacteria that lives symbiotically with legumes, carrying out nitrogen fixation (converting atmospheric N2 into ammonia).

questions.questionText: In a bacterial cell, what are 'Pili' used for?
options: Attaching to surfaces or other cells
questions.explanation: Pili are hair-like appendages that help bacteria stick to surfaces or exchange DNA.

questions.questionText: In Gram staining, if some bacteria retain the crystal violet after counter staining, then the bacteria is
questions.explanation:
The key feature of a Gram-positive bacterium is its thick peptidoglycan cell wall, which retains the initial stain, crystal violet, even after the decolorization step.

 Therefore, when counter-stained with safranin, these bacteria still appear purple/violet (retain the crystal violet).

questions.questionText: Which type of microorganism causes the disease 'Thrush'?
questions.explanation: Thrush is a yeast infection of the mouth caused by the fungus Candida albicans.

questions.questionText: A mutation that involves the insertion or deletion of a nucleotide, shifting the reading frame, is a:
questions.explanation: Frameshift mutations usually result in a completely different (and often non-functional) protein.

questions.questionText: Which organelle is the primary site of photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the organelles where light energy is converted into chemical energy during photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: Which of these is an example of an infectious protein?
questions.explanation: Prions are unusual because they are just proteins, yet they can cause infectious brain diseases like Mad Cow Disease.

questions.questionText: The cell wall of Archaea differs from Eubacteria because it lacks:
questions.explanation: Archaea do not have true peptidoglycan (murein); some have 'pseudomurein' or S-layers made of protein/glycoprotein.

questions.questionText: All of the following events happen in the reduction stages of the Calvin cycle EXCEPT
options: utilization of ATP and NADPH molecules.
conversion of 3 PGA into a sugar molecule.
donating of electrons to a 3C-intermediates to form G3P.
questions.explanation:
The reduction stage of the Calvin cycle involves ATP and NADPH being used to convert 3-phosphoglycerate (3-PGA) into glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P). 

The step of CO₂ combining with RuBP occurs in the carbon fixation stage, not the reduction stage, so it is the exception.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases is caused by food poisoning bacteria?
questions.explanation: Salmonellosis (Salmonella food poisoning) is a common gastrointestinal illness caused by Salmonella bacteria.

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of a bacterial flagellum?
questions.explanation: Flagella are whip-like tails that act like small motors to propel bacteria through liquid environments.

questions.questionText: Which protozoan causes Malaria in humans?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium species are apicomplexan protozoa transmitted by mosquitoes that cause malaria.

questions.questionText: The view of biochemical origin of life hypothesized that the first life forms appeared in warm, primitive ocean and were heterotrophic. Which one of the following statements can support this idea?
options: Life is the inherent property of the universe which permits unlimited existence
The appearance of dust of unknown source with microbial spores that can feed on organic molecules.
The formation of abundant organic molecules due to radiations and the absence of oxygen led to the primitive living organisms.
Resistant spores from meteorites reached to the earth and used organic molecules to survive in the environment.
questions.explanation:
The biochemical (primordial soup) hypothesis suggests that in the oxygen-free early oceans, energy from radiation, lightning, or UV light enabled the formation of organic molecules.

 These molecules accumulated and were used by heterotrophic primitive life forms.

questions.questionText: Viroids differ from viruses in that viroids:
questions.explanation: Viroids are small, circular, naked RNA molecules that infect plants; they do not have a protein coat (capsid).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an acellular infectious agent made only of protein?
questions.explanation: Prions are misfolded proteins that cause diseases like 'Mad Cow'; they contain no nucleic acid.

questions.questionText: What is the primary role of the stroma in chloroplasts?
options: To house the enzymes for the Calvin Cycle
questions.explanation: The stroma is the fluid environment where the light-independent reactions (sugar building) occur.

questions.questionText: Which of these protozoa is famous for having a 'slipper' shape?
questions.explanation: Paramecium has a distinct elongated, oval shape that resembles the sole of a slipper.

questions.questionText: Currently, natural resources are being depleted at increasing rate and waste materials are accumulated and discharged freely into water bodies. What is the best strategy to overcome these problems?
questions.explanation: Recycling directly addresses both issues: it reduces the need for new natural resources and decreases the amount of waste accumulated in the environment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences describes a virus?
questions.explanation:
A virus is an acellular particle (not a cell) consisting of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat.
 They are obligate intracellular parasites that lack the necessary machinery for metabolism or respiration. Therefore, the most accurate description is that it is not cellular.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a function of the human kidney?
questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by the pancreas, not the kidney.

questions.questionText: The term 'Dysbiosis' refers to:
options: The successful colonization of a host by a pathogen
An imbalance in the microbial community that can lead to disease
The symbiotic relationship between a fungus and an alga
The process of cleaning a surface with disinfectants
questions.explanation: Dysbiosis is a disruption to the normal microbiota, often linked to conditions like IBD, obesity, or C. difficile infections.

questions.questionText: Which protozoan group uses 'cilia' for both movement and feeding?
questions.explanation: Ciliates (Ciliophora), like Paramecium, have thousands of hair-like cilia that beat in waves.

questions.questionText: How do most bacteria move?
questions.explanation: Many bacteria use whip-like structures called flagella to rotate and move through liquids.

questions.questionText: Which hormone is produced by the pineal gland to regulate sleep-wake cycles?
questions.explanation: Melatonin production increases in the dark to signal the body it is time for sleep.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Archaea?
options: Presence of introns in some genes
questions.explanation: Archaea are generally not affected by antibiotics that target Eubacteria (like penicillin) because their cell walls and ribosomes are structurally different.

questions.questionText: Which part of the brain is the 'control center' for vital autonomic functions like heart rate and breathing?
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata, located in the brainstem, regulates essential life-support functions like heartbeat, respiration, and blood pressure.

questions.questionText: Find the correct path way of reflex are that prevents you from physical damage up on the sudden touching of hot plate.
options: Sensory neuron --> motor neuron --> spinal cord --> effector
Sensory neuron --> spinal cord --> motor neuron --> effector
Interneuron --> spinal cord --> motor neuron --> effector
questions.explanation:
In a reflex action, such as quickly withdrawing your hand from a hot plate, the sensory neuron detects the stimulus and sends a signal to the spinal cord, where it synapses with a motor neuron.

 The motor neuron then activates the effector (muscle) to produce a rapid response. This pathway bypasses the brain to ensure a fast protective reaction

questions.questionText: Which vitamin is produced by certain normal microbiota in the human large intestine?
questions.explanation: Bacteria like E. coli synthesize Vitamin K and some B vitamins, which are then absorbed by the human host.

questions.questionText: What is the net gain of ATP molecules from glycolysis alone?
questions.explanation: While glycolysis produces 4 ATP, it requires an initial investment of 2 ATP, resulting in a net gain of 2.

questions.questionText: Which part of the ear is responsible for equalizing pressure between the middle ear and the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx to balance air pressure.

questions.questionText: The bottleneck effect is a type of:
questions.explanation: The bottleneck effect occurs when a population size is drastically reduced by a disaster, leading to a random change in allele frequencies (drift).

questions.questionText: Which of these is a result of 'Sympathetic' nervous system activation?
questions.explanation: The sympathetic system dilates the airways to allow more oxygen into the body for physical activity.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a primary goal of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 13?
questions.explanation: SDG 13 specifically calls for urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.

questions.questionText: Which part of a neuron receives incoming signals from other cells?
questions.explanation: Dendrites are branch-like structures that catch signals and carry them to the cell body.

questions.questionText: In a scenario where a male black lion population left its terrestrial territory and joined a white female lion population in an isolated island to mate, there would be a
options: decrease in black lion population in the isolated island.
genetic variation in terrestrial population due to immigration.
random introduction of new alleles into the island population.
change in allele frequencies of terrestrial population but not in island.
questions.explanation:
When a male black lion migrates and mates with the white female lion population on the isolated island, new alleles are introduced into that population. This is an example of gene flow, which increases genetic variation in the receiving population.

 It does not affect the terrestrial population directly, nor does it specifically decrease black lions on the island.

questions.questionText: Which type of evidence for evolution focuses on the geographic distribution of species?
questions.explanation: Biogeography studies where species live now and where their ancestors lived in the past to understand evolutionary patterns.

questions.questionText: The 'Green Revolution' of the 1960s primarily relied on:
options: High-Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of wheat and rice
The use of CRISPR gene editing
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution used semi-dwarf, high-yielding seeds combined with irrigation and fertilizers to boost food production.

questions.questionText: Which genetic phenomenon is common for both bottleneck and founder effects?
options: High mutation rate that enhances adaptation
Genetic drift that reduces diversity in the population
Gene flow that increases inbreed and disease's resistance
Natural selection that results from gradual evolutionary changes
questions.explanation:
Both the bottleneck effect (a drastic reduction in population size) and the founder effect (a small group establishing a new population) involve genetic drift, which is a random change in allele frequencies.

 This leads to a reduction in genetic diversity** and can affect the population's ability to adapt, independent of natural selection or mutation rates.

questions.questionText: Microbes that cause disease only when the host's defenses are down are:
questions.explanation: Opportunistic pathogens take the 'opportunity' provided by a weak immune system to cause an infection.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is used in 'Gene Therapy'?
options: Using exercise to change your DNA
Using healthy genes to treat or prevent disease
Removing all genes from a patient
questions.explanation: Gene therapy involves inserting a functional gene into a patient's cells to replace a defective one.

questions.questionText: What is the function of ATP synthase?
options: To use a proton gradient to create ATP from ADP
questions.explanation: ATP synthase is an enzyme 'motor' that spins as protons flow through it, attaching a phosphate to ADP.

questions.questionText: What is 'Protoplast Fusion' in plant biotechnology?
options: Merging two cells that have had their cell walls removed
questions.explanation: Protoplast fusion allows for the creation of somatic hybrids between different plant species that cannot sexually cross.
